name: Tuk Tuk Thai
shortDescription: A pure-veg Thai kitchen that cooks the street food of Bangkok and Chiang Mai without fish sauce, egg or meat. Curry pastes pounded fresh every morning.
story: Tuk Tuk Thai started as a four-table place run by a Thai home cook and her Indian husband, who wanted the food of Bangkok's night markets without anything his vegetarian family could not eat. Fish sauce became salt and soy. Egg left the pad thai. Nothing else changed. Eleven years later the menu is twenty pages because they could not stop adding dishes.
awards: Condé Nast Traveller India, Top 50 Restaurants 2024
chefNote: Start with a salad or soup, then one curry with rice per two people, one noodle or wok dish, and share a dessert. That is how a Thai table eats. Do not order everything at once.

spiceGuide.label: Hot
spiceGuide.note: Proper Thai heat, you will reach for a drink

dietaryLegend.vegan: No dairy, no egg, no honey
dietaryLegend.jain-possible: Can be made without onion, garlic and root vegetables, ask when ordering
dietaryLegend.gluten-free: No wheat or soy sauce with wheat

welcome.greeting: Sawasdee ka. Twenty pages is a lot.
welcome.intro: I'm Noi, your table host. Three quick questions and I'll have you at the right plate. Or skip them and just ask me anything, in any language.

firstQuestion.question: First things first. How do you feel about chilli tonight?

hero.alt: Warm teak dining room with lanterns
A tuk-tuk ride through Bangkok at night
A Bangkok street food vendor at night

video.caption: Bangkok night market energy, the mood we cook from

sections.name: Small Plates
sections.blurb: Crisp, shareable, made for the first ten minutes at the table.

sections.name: Salads
sections.blurb: Bright, sour, crunchy. Thai salads wake the mouth up.

sections.name: Soups
sections.blurb: Fragrant broths built on lemongrass, galangal and lime leaf.

sections.name: Curries
sections.blurb: Coconut-milk curries from four regions, each a different colour and mood.

sections.name: Noodles & Wok
sections.blurb: Street-stall wok dishes, smoky and fast.

sections.name: Rice
sections.blurb: Fried rice from the wok and jasmine rice for the curries.

sections.name: Sweets
sections.blurb: Coconut, mango, banana. Thai sweets are gentle, never heavy.

sections.name: Drinks
sections.blurb: Cold, sweet, and built to calm the chilli.

dishes.name: Crispy Vegetable Spring Rolls
dishes.tagline: Shatter-crisp rolls of glass noodle, cabbage and carrot, with a sweet chilli dip.
dishes.description: Six golden rolls arrive standing in a bamboo basket with a small bowl of sweet chilli sauce. The wrapper is paper-thin and blistered, the inside is soft glass noodle, cabbage, carrot and black fungus with a hit of white pepper.
dishes.story: The Thai spring roll came up the Chao Phraya with Chinese traders and got lighter and crisper on the way. Ours are rolled every afternoon and fried to order.
dishes.tastesLike: A lighter, crisper cousin of the Indo-Chinese veg roll, with less filling and more crunch.
dishes.texture: Crackly outside, soft and slippery inside.
howToEat: Pick one up with your fingers, do not wait, they are best in the first five minutes.
Dip the end in the sweet chilli sauce, not the whole roll, so the wrapper stays crisp.
Two bites per roll. Wrap in a lettuce leaf with mint if you want it fresher.

reviews.quote: Crispiest spring rolls in the city, no exaggeration.
Perfect starter while you figure out the rest of the menu.

images.alt: Crispy vegetable spring rolls with sweet chilli dip
Vegetable spring rolls on a plate
Thai spring rolls cut to show the filling

dishes.name: Tofu Satay with Peanut Sauce
dishes.tagline: Turmeric-marinated tofu grilled on bamboo skewers, with a thick, warm peanut sauce.
dishes.description: Five skewers of firm tofu, marinated in turmeric, lemongrass and coconut milk, char-grilled so the edges catch. They come on a wooden board with a bowl of warm peanut sauce and a small cucumber-shallot pickle (ajat).
dishes.story: Satay is Indonesian by birth and Thai by adoption. The peanut sauce here is made from scratch with roasted peanuts, red curry paste and coconut cream.
dishes.tastesLike: Think paneer tikka's gentler cousin, with a peanut-chutney sauce that is sweeter and creamier.
dishes.texture: Firm and slightly chewy tofu with a smoky crust, thick silky sauce.
howToEat: Hold the skewer, dip a piece into the peanut sauce, then eat straight off the stick.
Take a bit of the cucumber pickle between skewers, it resets your palate.
Spoon leftover peanut sauce over jasmine rice later. Nobody will judge.

reviews.quote: The peanut sauce alone is worth the visit.
Smoky, not rubbery. Finally a tofu dish that converts people.

images.alt: Grilled tofu skewers with peanut sauce
Vegetable satay skewers on a plate

dishes.name: Thai Curry Puffs
dishes.tagline: Flaky spiral pastry filled with spiced potato, sweet corn and onion.
dishes.description: Four half-moon pastries with the signature flaky spiral crust. Inside is a soft mash of potato, sweet corn, onion and yellow curry powder. Served with a cool cucumber relish.
dishes.story: Karipap travelled from Portuguese Goa to Malaysia to Thailand. The filling is the closest thing on this menu to a samosa, which is exactly why first-timers love it.
dishes.tastesLike: A samosa that went to finishing school. Flakier pastry, sweeter and milder filling.
dishes.texture: Layers that flake apart, soft and creamy inside.
howToEat: Eat with your hands. Break one in half first so the steam escapes.
The cucumber relish is meant to go on top of each bite, like a chutney.
Pair with Thai iced tea if you want a full tea-time moment.

reviews.quote: Samosa lovers, start here.
That spiral crust is gorgeous and tastes even better.

images.alt: Flaky Thai curry puffs
A curry puff broken open to show the filling

dishes.name: Green Papaya Salad
dishes.tagline: Pounded green papaya with lime, palm sugar, chilli, peanuts and long beans. Loud and bright.
dishes.description: A heap of shredded raw green papaya, pounded in a clay mortar with cherry tomatoes, long beans, roasted peanuts, garlic and bird's eye chilli. Dressed with lime and palm sugar. It arrives on a shallow plate with a wedge of cabbage on the side.
dishes.story: Som tam is Isan's gift to the world. The Jay version swaps fish sauce for salt and soy so it stays pure vegetarian, and we pound each plate to order so you can set the heat.
dishes.serves: 1 as a main, 2 as a side
dishes.tastesLike: Imagine a kachumber that got serious: more sour, more crunch, real heat, with peanuts for comfort.
dishes.texture: Crunchy, juicy, with the pop of peanuts.
howToEat: Use a spoon and fork, Thai style: fork pushes, spoon carries.
Scoop with the raw cabbage wedge if you want crunch on crunch and less heat.
Eat it alongside sticky rice or a curry. It is a side that steals the show, not a solo act.
Ask for 1 chilli if you are unsure. 2 is medium. 4 is how Isan eats it.

reviews.quote: Asked for 2 chillies, cried happily. Order it.
Fresh and punchy. The peanuts make it.
Best som tam outside Bangkok, and I have had a lot of som tam.

images.alt: Green papaya salad with peanuts and tomato
Som tam on a plate
Som tam being pounded in a clay mortar

dishes.name: Green Mango Salad
dishes.tagline: Sour raw mango, toasted coconut, cashews and shallots in a lime-chilli dressing.
dishes.description: Julienned raw mango tossed with crisp fried shallots, toasted coconut flakes, roasted cashews and mint. The dressing is lime, palm sugar and a little chilli. Served chilled in a shallow bowl.
dishes.story: Thais eat raw mango with salt and chilli the way Indians eat it with salt and chilli. This salad is that instinct turned into a plate.
dishes.tastesLike: Raw mango with chaat masala energy, but with coconut and cashew doing the crunchy work.
dishes.texture: Crisp, juicy, with crunchy shallots and nuts.
howToEat: Toss once at the table so the crunchy bits do not sink.
Eat it first. It opens the appetite for everything after.
Great alongside the Massaman, the sour cuts the richness.

reviews.quote: Sour, sweet, crunchy. I think about this salad on Tuesdays.
A lovely cold start on a hot evening.

images.alt: Green mango salad with cashews and herbs

dishes.name: Tom Yum Mushroom Soup
dishes.tagline: Hot and sour broth with lemongrass, galangal, lime leaf and three kinds of mushroom.
dishes.description: A clear, reddish broth that smells of lemongrass before it reaches the table. Inside are oyster, button and straw mushrooms, cherry tomatoes and a handful of coriander. It comes in a deep bowl with a wide spoon, for one or to share.
dishes.story: Tom yum is the national soup of Thailand. Hed means mushroom. The 'nam sai' clear version is lighter than the creamy one, and it is how most Bangkok kitchens serve it.
dishes.tastesLike: A rasam that discovered lemongrass. Sharp, hot, aromatic and very light.
dishes.texture: Thin broth, meaty mushrooms, soft tomato.
howToEat: Do not eat the lemongrass stalks, galangal slices or lime leaves. They are for flavour, push them aside.
Sip the broth first, then go for the mushrooms with the spoon.
Squeeze the extra lime wedge in if you want it sharper.
Pour a ladle over jasmine rice if you ordered rice. That is a very Thai move.

reviews.quote: Cleared my sinuses and my mood.
Light enough to have before a curry. Perfectly balanced.

images.alt: Tom yum mushroom soup in a bowl
Clear tom yum with mushrooms and herbs
Tom yum with tofu

dishes.name: Coconut Galangal Soup with Tofu
dishes.tagline: Creamy coconut broth, gentle galangal warmth, silken tofu and mushrooms. The soft landing.
dishes.description: A pale, creamy soup in a deep bowl. Coconut milk simmered with galangal, lemongrass and lime leaf, with cubes of silken tofu and mushrooms. Finished with lime and a few coriander leaves. Barely any chilli.
dishes.story: Tom kha is tom yum's calm sibling. Same aromatics, but coconut milk rounds everything off. It is the soup we hand to anyone nervous about Thai food.
dishes.tastesLike: A thin, fragrant coconut stew. If you like a Kerala-style coconut curry, this is its soup form.
dishes.texture: Silky and creamy, soft tofu, tender mushrooms.
howToEat: Push the galangal slices and lemongrass to the side, they are too woody to eat.
Spoon the tofu gently, it is silken and breaks easily.
Great with a side of jasmine rice if you want to turn it into a light meal.

reviews.quote: The gentlest, most comforting bowl. My go-to when I am tired.
Brought my parents, they loved this and asked for it again.

images.alt: Creamy tom kha coconut soup
Tom kha in a bowl with herbs
Coconut galangal soup close-up

dishes.name: Green Curry with Tofu & Thai Eggplant
dishes.tagline: The famous one. Fresh green chilli and basil in coconut milk, with tofu, Thai eggplant and bamboo shoot.
dishes.description: A pale green, glossy curry in a ceramic bowl, served with a plate of jasmine rice. Tofu, small round Thai eggplants, bamboo shoots and sweet basil float in a coconut sauce that smells of lemongrass and lime leaf. Hot, but the sweetness catches it.
dishes.story: Khiao wan means 'green sweet'. The paste is pounded fresh here from green bird's eye chilli, galangal, coriander root and kaffir lime zest. It is the dish most people picture when they hear 'Thai food'.
dishes.tastesLike: Nothing quite Indian. Closest is a coconut-based curry with a green-chilli chutney stirred in, plus a herbal, almost citrus perfume.
dishes.texture: Thin-to-medium sauce, soft tofu, slightly bitter crunchy eggplant.
howToEat: Spoon the curry over the rice, a little at a time, rather than pouring it all in.
Eat with a spoon, fork in the other hand to push. No knife needed.
The small round things are Thai eggplants, eat them, they are slightly bitter on purpose.
Order 'mild' if you are heat-shy. The flavour stays, the burn goes.

reviews.quote: Tastes like Bangkok. The basil at the end is everything.
I order this every single time. Mild version is still full of flavour.
Fresh paste, you can tell. Not from a jar.

images.alt: Green curry served with jasmine rice
Green and yellow curry side by side
Fresh green curry paste in a mortar

video.caption: Inside a vegetarian Thai kitchen in Bangkok

dishes.name: Red Curry with Tofu & Pumpkin
dishes.tagline: Deeper and smokier than green. Dried red chilli paste, coconut milk, sweet pumpkin and tofu.
dishes.description: A brick-red curry, a shade thicker than the green, with cubes of pumpkin, tofu, red pepper and basil. Served in a bowl with jasmine rice on the side. The pumpkin sweetens it as it cooks.
dishes.story: Phet means spicy, and historically this was the hot one. Dried red chillies give it depth instead of the green's freshness. The pumpkin is our kitchen's touch for the Indian palate.
dishes.tastesLike: Closer to home than the green: think of a coconut-rich, red-chilli gravy with a sweet vegetable in it.
dishes.texture: Medium-bodied sauce, melting pumpkin, firm tofu.
howToEat: Mash a piece of pumpkin into the sauce on your spoon, it makes the curry creamier.
Spoon over rice bit by bit. Thai curries are eaten with rice, never alone.
Finish with a sip of something cold, the red curry builds slowly.

reviews.quote: Pumpkin in red curry is genius, it sweetens every bite.
Spicier than green but rounder. My favourite of the two.

images.alt: Red curry with tofu
Red curry served with rice
Red curry in a bowl

dishes.name: Massaman Curry with Potato & Peanuts
dishes.tagline: Mild, sweet, cinnamon-scented. The curry that tastes like it already knows you.
dishes.description: A warm brown curry, thick and glossy, with soft potato chunks, onion, roasted peanuts and a cinnamon stick resting on top. Served with jasmine rice. Almost no chilli heat, lots of warmth from spices.
dishes.story: Massaman came to Thailand with Persian and Indian Muslim traders in the 1600s, which is why it has cardamom, cinnamon and cumin. CNN once named it the world's most delicious dish. It is the bridge between Indian and Thai cooking.
dishes.tastesLike: A gentle Thai cousin of a korma, with tamarind sweetness and coconut instead of cream.
dishes.texture: Thick, velvety sauce, fluffy potato, crunchy peanuts.
howToEat: Leave the cinnamon stick and cardamom pods on the side, they are not meant to be eaten.
This one loves rice. Spoon generously, it is thick enough to coat every grain.
Add a squeeze of lime if you want to lift the sweetness.

reviews.quote: If you are scared of Thai food, this is your door in. Then you never leave.
Rich, sweet, comforting. My kids demolished it.
The potatoes soak up everything. Incredible.

images.alt: Vegetable massaman curry with rice
Massaman curry with potato and peanuts

dishes.name: Yellow Curry with Vegetables
dishes.tagline: Turmeric-gold, mild, with potato, carrot and onion. Thailand's softest curry.
dishes.description: A golden, mellow curry in a bowl, with potato, carrot, onion and baby corn in a thick coconut sauce. Served with jasmine rice and a little cucumber relish.
dishes.story: Kari is the Thai pronunciation of 'curry'. This is the Thai south's take on an Indian curry: turmeric, cumin and coriander in coconut milk. The relish on the side is the traditional partner.
dishes.tastesLike: The most Indian-tasting dish on the menu: a mild coconut sabzi with a Thai perfume.
dishes.texture: Thick sauce, soft vegetables.
howToEat: Spoon over rice. Try a bite with a spoonful of the cucumber relish, the sourness is the point.
Mild by default. Ask for extra chilli on the side if you want it.

reviews.quote: Comfort food. Safe, warm, lovely.
Got the Jain version, they handled it without fuss.

images.alt: Yellow curry with vegetables
Yellow curry served with rice

dishes.name: Chiang Mai Curry Noodles
dishes.tagline: Northern Thai coconut curry broth over egg-free noodles, topped with a crispy noodle nest.
dishes.description: A bowl of soft flat noodles in a golden, curry-rich coconut broth, crowned with a tangle of crispy fried noodles. On the side: pickled mustard greens, sliced shallots, lime and chilli oil. It looks dramatic and eats like a hug.
dishes.story: Khao soi is Chiang Mai's signature, with Burmese and Yunnanese roots. We make it with tofu and oyster mushrooms. The crunchy top is the whole experience.
dishes.tastesLike: If a mild red curry and a noodle soup had a child, with a crunchy crown. Faintly like a coconut-based Burmese khow suey.
dishes.texture: Soft noodles, rich broth, shatteringly crispy top.
howToEat: Squeeze the lime and add the shallots and pickled greens before you start. They are not garnish, they balance the richness.
Eat the crispy noodles early, before they soften.
Chopsticks for noodles, spoon for broth. Slurping is fine.
Chilli oil is strong. Half a teaspoon first.

reviews.quote: That crispy noodle top is a drama I will pay for every week.
Rich, comforting, a complete meal in one bowl.

images.alt: Khao soi with crispy noodle topping
Khao soi curry noodles
Khao soi with condiments

dishes.name: Pad Thai with Tofu
dishes.tagline: Stir-fried rice noodles in tamarind sauce, with tofu, bean sprouts, chives and crushed peanuts.
dishes.description: A plate of thin rice noodles glazed in a sweet-sour tamarind sauce, tossed in a hot wok with tofu, bean sprouts and garlic chives. On the side: crushed peanuts, chilli flakes, a lime wedge and extra bean sprouts, so you season it yourself.
dishes.story: Pad Thai was promoted by the Thai government in the 1940s to build a national identity around rice noodles. Ours uses tamarind and palm sugar, no ketchup, no fish sauce.
dishes.tastesLike: Sweet-and-sour noodles with a tamarind tang. If you like the sweetness of a Hakka noodle but want more character, this is it.
dishes.texture: Slippery soft noodles, crunchy sprouts and peanuts.
howToEat: Season it yourself: squeeze the lime, add peanuts, then a pinch of chilli flakes. Toss and taste.
Fork and spoon, or chopsticks. Both are correct.
Eat it hot. Pad Thai does not improve with waiting.

reviews.quote: Not overly sweet like most places. Proper tamarind.
The safe choice that is actually great.

images.alt: Pad thai with tofu and vegetables
Vegan pad thai with peanuts and lime
Vegan pad thai plate

dishes.name: Pad See Ew
dishes.tagline: Wide rice noodles, dark soy, Chinese broccoli and tofu, charred in a screaming-hot wok.
dishes.description: Broad, chewy rice noodles stained dark with sweet soy, with pieces of Chinese broccoli and tofu. Smoky edges from the wok. No sauce pooling, just glossy noodles on a plate.
dishes.story: See ew means soy sauce. This is the Thai-Chinese comfort noodle, the one Bangkok office workers eat at lunch. The smokiness, 'wok hei', is the thing to taste for.
dishes.tastesLike: Closest to a good Indo-Chinese chilli-garlic noodle minus the chilli, with wider, chewier noodles and more smoke.
dishes.texture: Soft, chewy, slightly crisp edges.
howToEat: Add chilli vinegar from the condiment set, a teaspoon. It cuts the sweetness.
Chopsticks work best for wide noodles, but a fork is fine.
Order it mild and it is the safest hot dish on the menu.

reviews.quote: Smoky and savoury, zero heat. My non-spicy friend's favourite.
Wok flavour is real here.

images.alt: Pad see ew with wide rice noodles
Pad see ew plate
Pad see ew close-up

dishes.name: Drunken Noodles
dishes.tagline: Wide noodles with holy basil, fresh chilli, garlic and vegetables. The loud, hot wok dish.
dishes.description: Wide rice noodles tossed with lots of holy basil, green peppercorns, chilli, garlic, baby corn, bell pepper and tofu. Glossy, dark, fragrant. It smells like a street stall.
dishes.story: Nobody agrees why it is called drunken. Best theory: it is what you cook at midnight to sober up. There is no alcohol in it, just enough chilli to wake you.
dishes.tastesLike: A Thai answer to a spicy Schezwan noodle, but herbal instead of saucy, with holy basil doing the talking.
dishes.texture: Chewy noodles, crisp vegetables, lots of leaf.
howToEat: Eat the basil leaves, they are the dish.
Keep a cold drink nearby. The chilli is fresh and arrives late.
Ask for 'medium' if you are unsure. 'Thai hot' is not a dare, it is a warning.

reviews.quote: Spicy, basil-heavy, perfect. Ordered Thai hot and survived.
My favourite noodle on the menu, every time.

images.alt: Drunken noodles with vegetables and tofu
Vegetarian drunken noodles
Pad kee mao close-up

video.caption: A vegetarian drunken noodle cook-along, wok and all

dishes.name: Flash-fried Morning Glory
dishes.tagline: Water spinach flamed in the wok with garlic, chilli and soybean paste. Thirty seconds, done.
dishes.description: A tangle of bright green water spinach stems and leaves, glossy with garlic and fermented soybean paste, with slices of red chilli. Served on a plate, meant to be shared like a sabzi.
dishes.story: Fai daeng means 'red fire'. At street stalls the cook tosses this in a wok that flares up to the ceiling. It is the vegetable side every Thai table orders.
dishes.tastesLike: A garlicky stir-fried saag with crunch and a salty-umami kick, more like a Chinese greens dish than anything Indian.
dishes.texture: Crunchy stems, silky leaves.
howToEat: Share it. Put it in the middle like a vegetable side.
Eat with jasmine rice and a curry. It is the green that balances the meal.
Eat the stems too, they are the best part.

reviews.quote: Garlicky and crunchy. Finally a green I want to order.
Perfect side to the green curry.

images.alt: Stir-fried morning glory with garlic and chilli

dishes.name: Pineapple Fried Rice
dishes.tagline: Served in a hollowed pineapple: curry-scented rice with pineapple, cashews, raisins and peas.
dishes.description: Half a pineapple, scooped out and filled with golden fried rice. Chunks of pineapple, cashews, raisins, peas and spring onion, with a dusting of yellow curry powder. Sweet, savoury, and very photogenic.
dishes.story: A Thai-Chinese restaurant invention from the 1970s tourism boom, now a Thai classic in its own right. Everyone photographs it. Nobody regrets ordering it.
dishes.serves: 1 as a meal, 2 as a side
dishes.tastesLike: A sweeter, fruitier pulao with a light curry scent. If you like raisins in your biryani, you are home.
dishes.texture: Fluffy rice, juicy pineapple, crunchy cashew.
howToEat: Take the photo first, we know.
Eat from the pineapple with a spoon, it keeps the rice warm and perfumed.
Great with the red curry on the side, sweet and hot together.

reviews.quote: Kids go crazy for the pineapple bowl. Adults too, honestly.
Sweet-savoury done right. Cashews in every bite.

images.alt: Pineapple fried rice served in a pineapple
Fried rice in a hollowed pineapple
Thai-style pineapple fried rice

dishes.name: Holy Basil Fried Rice with Tofu
dishes.tagline: Street-stall fried rice with holy basil, garlic, chilli and crispy tofu. Bangkok's lunch.
dishes.description: A mound of wok-fried jasmine rice flecked with holy basil, garlic, fresh chilli and crispy tofu cubes, with a wedge of lime and cucumber slices on the side.
dishes.story: Kaphrao is Thailand's most-ordered lunch. It is what you ask for when you cannot decide. The holy basil is peppery and clove-like, nothing like Italian basil.
dishes.tastesLike: A spicy garlic fried rice with a herb you have not met before. Nearer to a chilli-garlic fried rice than to anything Indian.
dishes.texture: Fluffy rice, crispy tofu, soft wilted basil.
howToEat: Squeeze the lime over everything first.
Eat with a spoon, it is a one-plate meal.
Cucumber slices are there to cool your mouth between bites.

reviews.quote: Simple, hot, fast. My weekday order.
Holy basil is addictive. Order medium.

images.alt: Tofu basil fried rice
Wok-fried rice with vegetables

dishes.name: Steamed Jasmine Rice
dishes.tagline: Fragrant Thai jasmine rice, steamed soft. The quiet partner to every curry.
dishes.description: A bowl of long-grain jasmine rice, slightly sticky and faintly floral. One bowl is enough for one curry.
dishes.story: Hom mali means 'jasmine fragrance'. Thai rice is softer and stickier than basmati on purpose, so it holds curry.
dishes.tastesLike: Softer and more fragrant than basmati, less fluffy, slightly clingy.
dishes.texture: Soft, a little sticky.
howToEat: Spoon curry over a little rice at a time. Do not drown it.
One bowl per person per curry is the usual ratio.

reviews.quote: Perfectly cooked every time.

images.alt: Steamed jasmine rice

dishes.name: Mango Sticky Rice
dishes.tagline: Warm coconut sticky rice, cold ripe mango, salted coconut cream, crunchy mung beans.
dishes.description: Slices of sweet ripe mango fanned beside a small mound of glutinous rice that has been steamed and soaked in sweetened coconut milk. A spoon of salted coconut cream on top and a sprinkle of toasted mung beans. Warm rice, cool mango.
dishes.story: Thailand's most famous dessert, originally a hot-season treat when mangoes peak. The salt in the coconut cream is not a mistake, it makes the mango taste sweeter.
dishes.tastesLike: A coconut kheer that set into rice, next to the best mango of the season.
dishes.texture: Chewy, sticky rice, soft mango, crunchy beans.
howToEat: Get a bit of rice and a bit of mango on the same spoon. Never separately.
Drag the spoon through the salted coconut cream on the way.
Eat it while the rice is still warm, the contrast is the whole point.

reviews.quote: I came for the curry and left thinking only about this.
Warm rice, cold mango, salty cream. Perfect.
Best dessert in town. Fight me.

images.alt: Mango sticky rice with coconut cream
Mango sticky rice plate
Mango sticky rice with coconut ice cream

dishes.name: Fresh Coconut Ice Cream
dishes.tagline: Churned from fresh coconut milk, served in a coconut shell with roasted peanuts and sweet corn.
dishes.description: Two scoops of pale coconut ice cream in a young coconut shell, with soft coconut flesh at the bottom, a scattering of roasted peanuts and a spoon of sweet corn kernels. Yes, corn. Trust it.
dishes.story: Coconut ice cream is sold from carts all over Bangkok, with toppings like sticky rice, corn and peanuts. The corn is a 1950s Bangkok habit that stuck.
dishes.tastesLike: Tender coconut and malai kulfi had a child, lighter than kulfi, cleaner than regular ice cream.
dishes.texture: Smooth and icy, crunchy peanuts, soft corn.
howToEat: Scrape the young coconut flesh off the inside of the shell with each spoonful.
Try one bite with corn before you decide you do not like corn on ice cream.

reviews.quote: Corn on ice cream sounded wrong. It is right.
Light, fresh, not sugary. Ideal after a spicy meal.

images.alt: Coconut ice cream in a coconut shell
Coconut ice cream with toppings

dishes.name: Coconut Pancake Bites
dishes.tagline: Little half-domes of rice-flour and coconut batter, crisp outside, custardy inside, with spring onion or corn.
dishes.description: Eight bite-sized pancakes cooked in a cast-iron dimpled pan. The edges are crisp, the centre is soft coconut custard. Topped with spring onion, sweet corn or taro. Served warm in a banana-leaf cup.
dishes.story: A street breakfast that moonlights as dessert. The savoury spring onion topping on a sweet coconut base confuses everyone for one bite and then makes complete sense.
dishes.tastesLike: Like a tiny appam that turned into a custard. Sweet-salty, coconutty, a little crisp.
dishes.texture: Crisp shell, molten custardy middle.
howToEat: Eat in one bite while warm. They collapse if you wait.
Pick with fingers or a toothpick. No cutlery needed.

reviews.quote: Tiny, warm, custardy. I ordered two rounds.
Reminded me of appam with coconut milk. Lovely.

images.alt: Khanom krok coconut pancakes in banana-leaf cups
Khanom krok on a woven tray

dishes.name: Banana Roti
dishes.tagline: Crispy street roti folded over caramelised banana, cut into squares, drizzled with condensed milk and chocolate.
dishes.description: A thin, stretched roti pan-fried in butter with sliced banana inside, folded into a parcel, cut into nine squares and finished with condensed milk and a zigzag of chocolate. Served on a paper-lined plate like the street stalls.
dishes.story: Thai roti came with Indian Muslim traders and became a night-market dessert. Yes, it is basically a sweet paratha, and it is unbeatable.
dishes.tastesLike: A sweet, crisp paratha stuffed with banana. You already know you like this.
dishes.texture: Crisp and flaky, soft caramel banana inside.
howToEat: Toothpick or fingers, square by square.
Eat fast, it is crispest in the first minutes.
Share it. It is sweeter than it looks.

reviews.quote: Pure night-market joy on a plate.

dishes.name: Bananas in Warm Coconut Milk
dishes.tagline: Ripe banana simmered gently in sweet, lightly salted coconut milk. The simplest, kindest dessert here.
dishes.description: A small bowl of warm coconut milk with soft pieces of banana, sweetened with palm sugar and a pinch of salt. Served warm, sometimes with a few pandan leaves for scent.
dishes.story: The name means 'bananas ordained as nuns', because the pale coconut milk looks like white robes. Thai grandmothers make this. It takes ten minutes and fixes most things.
dishes.tastesLike: A banana payasam with coconut milk, thinner and warmer, less sweet.
dishes.texture: Soft banana, silky warm milk.
howToEat: Spoon it like a soup, warm.
If you want a bit of crunch, ask for toasted sesame on top.

dishes.name: Thai Iced Tea
dishes.tagline: Strong spiced black tea over ice, with condensed milk floating on top in a bright orange swirl.
dishes.description: A tall glass packed with ice, deep orange tea with star anise and tamarind notes, and a layer of milk poured over the top. Stir and it turns the colour of a sunset.
dishes.story: The orange colour comes from the Thai tea blend itself. It was built to tame chilli, which is why every table in Bangkok has one.
dishes.tastesLike: A cold, very sweet masala chai with a smoky edge. Think chai, iced, with condensed milk.
dishes.texture: Icy, creamy.
howToEat: Stir before the first sip so the milk layer mixes in.
Ask for 'less sweet' if you are used to sugar-free chai, the default is dessert-level sweet.
Order it before the food, it arrives fast and helps with any chilli.

dishes.name: Lemongrass & Ginger Cooler
dishes.tagline: Fresh lemongrass and ginger, lightly sweetened, served ice cold. Pale green and clean.
dishes.description: A tall glass of pale green lemongrass infusion with a hint of ginger and lime, over ice. Not very sweet, very refreshing.
dishes.story: Nam takrai is what Thai homes serve guests on hot afternoons. It calms the stomach and cuts through rich coconut curries.
dishes.tastesLike: Like a cold lemongrass tea or a lighter nimbu pani with a ginger kick.
dishes.texture: Light, icy.
howToEat: Sip between bites of a rich curry, it resets your palate.
Ask for 'no sugar' if you want it purely herbal.
